Title: Workspace navigation
Text: The workspace lists systems granted to your signed-in account. Inventory System manages items, sets and requests; IT Call Monitoring tracks support tickets; Request/s Portal submits and follows requests; Consumable Management handles models, exchanges and refills; Borrow Items tracks loans and returns; Reports shows reporting views; Repair Technician Portal manages repairs; Admin Portal manages authorized account and configuration tasks. Ask Yakumi from any module using Ctrl+Shift+Y. Yakumi only reads information.

Title: Your identity and access
Text: Your account identity, linked employee and organizational details are loaded at login. A department account represents a department, not one employee. Workspace visibility follows portal permissions; pages and categories can be further restricted. Individual overrides take precedence over role defaults. Ask 'who am I?' or 'what can I access?' to inspect the current session. Ask an administrator to review missing access; Yakumi cannot grant it.

Title: Check item stock
Text: Open Inventory System and choose Items to search by name, model or serial number. Catalog records and physical quantities are different: several matching records can each hold stock. Yakumi displays a matching record count separately from the sum of available units. Inactive and archived item stock is excluded by default. Specify a model or category to narrow the lookup. Lowest-stock ordering lists small quantities first; it does not define a reorder threshold.

Title: Inventory movements and audit
Text: Inventory movements record posted quantities and entry types, with related item, request and set references. A sum of posted movement quantities is not the same as current available stock. Use Items for current stock, Inventory for postings, and Item Movement Audit or Ownership History to investigate a specific item. Keep the record type and date scope visible when comparing movement counts.

Title: Sets and equipment ownership
Text: Open Sets to inspect a set and its equipment. Yakumi follows the Sets grid: the employee comes from the first linked request, while current branch and department come from the set. This employee is not proof of the equipment's latest individual custodian; use Ownership History to inspect recorded transfers. Ask for 'my equipment' or 'SET-123 contents' with that scope in mind. Borrowed equipment belongs to the separate Borrow Items lifecycle; a borrow is not an ownership transfer.

Title: Assets and serial numbers
Text: Asset records identify tracked equipment through item links, serial numbers, model numbers and vendors. Use the Assets or Fixed Assets views available to your account and provide a serial or model to disambiguate equipment. An asset count, item catalog count and stock-unit total measure different things. Yakumi labels its source instead of treating these counts as interchangeable.

Title: Warranty checks
Text: Warranty information comes from the item's warranty dates and, in some desktop views, applicable invoice/set dates. Specify the item or serial and read the returned source and end date. Yakumi's warranty lookup labels item warranty records; it does not assert vendor coverage or eligibility beyond recorded dates. License and subscription renewals are separate from hardware warranty coverage.

Title: Submit and follow a request
Text: Open Request/s Portal to submit a request using the appropriate item or consumable workflow. Follow its approval and fulfillment in the portal. A request reference identifies a request line; a grouped submission can contain several lines. Use 'my requests' or give a REQ reference in Yakumi. Approval and physical fulfillment are separate stages. Yakumi can explain the steps and read their records but cannot submit, approve or issue items.

Title: Outstanding and partially fulfilled requests
Text: Requested quantity and issued quantity determine remaining fulfillment. A partially fulfilled line has some quantity issued and some remaining. Dispatched sets count as fulfilled in the desktop fulfillment view even when older issued-quantity data is incomplete. Inactive, rejected and cancelled records do not belong in the outstanding queue. A pending label alone does not prove a specific blocker; inspect authorization, issuance and set status before explaining the cause.

Title: Request approval and authorization
Text: Request authorizations track Pending, Approved, Rejected and Used states. They identify the requester and routed approver independently of inventory fulfillment. An approved authorization can later be consumed by its request workflow. When approval appears blocked, inspect the assigned approver and actual authorization status; do not assume a reason from the label alone. Request/s Portal exposes personal authorizations, while authorized consumable staff can manage the operational queue.

Title: Consumable model availability
Text: Ink, toner and print-head consumables are grouped by ConsumableModel. Availability is based on active item stock linked to the model; it is not pooled merely because names look similar. Supply the model and category when checking stock. CartridgeModel is a separate grouping with brand-new and refilled stock rules. Duplicate catalog rows and model totals should not be confused with distinct physical models.

Title: Brand-new and refilled cartridges
Text: Consumable Management handles cartridge models and exchanges. Brand-new issuable stock uses active cartridge items whose RefillStatus is empty. Refilled issuable stock uses active items marked Available. IT-custody empties are excluded from issuable stock. Yakumi reports condition totals separately; returned empties are not ready-to-issue stock. Provide the model and requested condition when checking availability.

Title: Refill batch lifecycle
Text: Cartridge returns can be collected into vendor batches and sent for refill. Batch status, sent quantity and returned quantity describe the vendor lifecycle. Batch purpose distinguishes refill, sale and disposal; their outcomes are not interchangeable. Completion and restocking must follow the desktop workflow so received stock is correctly linked and marked. Yakumi can list batches and quantities but cannot receive stock or close a batch.

Title: Unfulfilled cartridge exchanges
Text: An exchange can record requested full cartridges, issued full cartridges, returned empties and the outstanding quantity. Good and damaged empties have separate handling. An empty-return count is not an issued-full count. Use the unfulfilled exchange queue to inspect what remains and the exchange's recorded status. Yakumi reads those quantities; authorized staff perform fulfillment in the desktop.

Title: Report and follow an IT issue
Text: Open IT Call Monitoring to record or inspect a support issue when your account has access. A ticket records its caller, issue, priority, status and assignment. Use its TCK reference in Yakumi for an exact lookup, or ask for your created/assigned tickets. Add evidence and solution notes through the ticket workflow. Yakumi has no verified support phone or email to invent and cannot create or change a ticket.

Title: Ticket statuses and reporting definitions
Text: Ticket statuses include Pending, In Progress, Escalated, Resolved (Temporary), Solved, Closed, Reopened and Forwarded to Repair. Temporary resolution is not interchangeable with final solution. An exact Solved count uses that status alone. Completion reports can apply a different documented history-based definition. Always identify whether a count measures current status, tickets created during a period, or status changes during a period. A status label alone does not establish the reason a ticket is waiting.

Title: Ticket assignment and personal scope
Text: A ticket can link both an assigned user account and an assigned employee. Personal ticket queries include records created by or assigned to the signed-in account or linked employee. A caller name is not reliable proof of account ownership. Specify an employee name when filtering another authorized assignment; ambiguous names need clarification. Portal access controls whether ticket records are visible.

Title: Reminders, escalations and email logs
Text: Ticket reminders and escalations follow configured settings and activity/status rules. Email logs distinguish Sent, Skipped and Failed outcomes; a missing row is different from a logged failure. Inspect ticket activity and email logs before attributing a delivery problem to SMTP or assignment. Settings and credentials are managed only in authorized configuration screens. Yakumi must not expose credentials or claim an email was sent without a recorded result.

Title: Borrow equipment
Text: Open Borrow Items to select eligible equipment and a valid borrower, then complete the desktop confirmation. A borrow record links the item, borrower, encoder and timestamp. Only one open loan is allowed per item. Ask 'my borrowed items' for loans linked to your employee ID. A department account or an account without an employee link must not be guessed into another person's loans. Yakumi cannot record a loan.

Title: Returns and borrow aging
Text: A return updates the original borrow lifecycle with its returner, encoder and returned timestamp. Open records have no returned timestamp. Borrow aging measures elapsed time since borrowing; the checked schema has no due date or expected return date, so Yakumi cannot classify a loan as overdue. Use 'my returned borrows' or 'borrow history' to separate returned equipment from open loans. Yakumi cannot record a return.

Title: Repair ticket lifecycle
Text: Repair Technician Portal tracks equipment problems, assignment, diagnosis, repair work, testing and recorded conclusions. Ticket states include Waiting, Diagnosing, Repairing, AwaitingParts, Testing, Completed and Unrepairable. A repair ticket and an IT support ticket have separate references and lifecycles even when linked. Read the diagnosis and recorded resolution before explaining an outcome. Yakumi can retrieve repair information but cannot change technician work or conclusions.

Title: Repair parts and service history
Text: Repair parts have their own status and severity, separate from the parent repair ticket. Recorded part states include WaitingDiagnosis, Diagnosing, Repairing, WaitingParts, Testing, Repaired and CannotRepair. Inspect parts and ticket history to understand progress; ticket completion does not imply every part used the same status path. Replacement, disposition and sign-off decisions belong to the authorized repair workflow.

Title: Invoice amounts and financial breakdowns
Text: Invoices are invoice sets with header and line information. Open Invoices to inspect document number, purchase order, organization, dates and the recorded subtotal, VAT, withholding, discount and amount due. Group overrides and calculation precedence belong to the application's invoice logic. Yakumi reads authoritative stored/view totals instead of recomputing tax precedence from partial rows. An invoice count, invoice-line count and summed amount are different measures.

Title: Invoice grouping and parent tags
Text: Invoice items display Sub-Type Group outside Parent Tag, then Category and individual rows. Sub-Type groups represent Contract, Subscription, License or Services and can carry financial/date overrides. Parent tags are independent free-text organization and do not provide VAT, withholding, discount or date overrides. An item can belong to both. Ask for invoice contents or group summaries while preserving the grouping dimension and source totals.

Title: Invoice Sub Groups and license review
Text: Invoice Sub Groups stages grouped items before or after their generated invoice, with completed and not-completed views. InvoiceBuilder can register completed groups back into staging; parent tags do not have the same staging concept. Invoice License Review and Non-Licensed Invoices are distinct review screens. Their eligibility rules should be checked in those views rather than inferred from invoice amount or name. Yakumi can explain navigation and retrieve registered invoice information.

Title: Renewals and expiry windows
Text: Renewal records track status, period dates, renewal count and recorded amount. Specify a product, part number or reference and a date window. Expired records have end dates before the relevant day; upcoming records have end dates within the stated window. History rows and unique contracts/assets are different counts, so Yakumi labels renewal-record totals. Hardware warranty is a separate lookup. Yakumi cannot renew a license or change a period.

Title: Receipts and supporting documents
Text: Receipts store supplier and SI, DR and PO references and can link to sets and supporting document images. Search the appropriate document reference before assuming two similar records are the same receipt. Yakumi can retrieve receipt metadata but does not read image contents or expose stored attachment bytes. Open the authorized receipt view to inspect the supporting document.

Title: Read reports and compare periods
Text: Choose the report and its date/filter definition before comparing totals. Current status snapshots, activity during a period, record counts and physical-unit sums answer different questions. Compare like-for-like metrics and consistent units. Yakumi can show grouped summaries and differences between supported periods; it displays the applied source and scope. An unsupported report definition should be clarified instead of approximated from unrelated rows.

Title: Archive visibility
Text: Archived and inactive are separate states. Archive records identify an entity, reason and archival time; normal operational pages commonly exclude archived data. Ask explicitly for archived records when investigating historical visibility. Existing archive permissions still apply. Yakumi cannot archive, restore or delete anything. Counts from the archive registry measure archive entries, not available stock.

Title: Employees and organization master data
Text: Inventory master-data pages maintain employees, companies, branches, departments and vendors. Employee title display uses the Title Code, while Position is a separate field. Search with all meaningful name parts or an employee number; one matching name fragment is not enough to identify a person. An inactive record can remain in historical transactions. Changes and imports must be performed in the authorized desktop pages, not through Yakumi.

Title: Account and permission administration
Text: Admin Portal access is restricted to Developer or Super Admin. Account and permission screens can further restrict access. Portal rights, page rights, item-category rights and action rights are distinct. Individual overrides take precedence over role baselines; a denied role baseline applies unless an individual grant overrides it. Yakumi can inspect permitted account/role information and explain access, but never shows passwords, hashes, salts or protected credentials and cannot grant permissions.

Title: User activity and audit information
Text: User Activity records the actor, action, entity, description and timestamp captured by the application. Use the entity or actor and a date window to narrow investigation. A missing log entry does not prove that no external change occurred. Yakumi reads existing activity and performs no audit-table writes. More detailed item movements or ticket history should be inspected in their corresponding sources.

Title: Configuration and system administration
Text: Admin Portal groups account management, approver management, department accounts/history, reference-data acronyms, holidays and email/SMTP administration. Use the relevant page to inspect configuration; read its validation and access requirements before changing it. Troubleshooting guidance must distinguish application settings from actual delivery logs. Yakumi does not fetch credential values, run migrations, contact devices, send email or modify configuration.
